species.name: Causal mechanism linking action to stated goal
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment explains a specific causal chain connecting the proposed rule/action to the outcome it claims will follow, rather than merely asserting a stance. A 10: the comment traces an explicit mechanism (e.g., 'X causes Y because Z') with enough specificity that a reader could evaluate whether the logic holds. A 0: the comment states support/opposition or a general value ('this is important', 'this is bad') with no explanation of how the action produces the claimed effect.
species.rationale: R03 traces a specific hydrological/geological chain (upstream forestland destruction -> loss of vegetative cover -> flooding, landslide, and debris-flow risk to downstream owners for decades) and R10 explains why cecal-plug controls reduce non-visible fecal contamination and why 'you can't test safety into food' argues for validated process controls over testing -- both dense_high_card_low rows where the mechanism itself is the substantive content a checklist of topic/stance tags would miss. Contrast R09 and R53, which assert conclusions ('this will increase safety', 'these crops require more pesticide, how can you not know this') without ever stating the mechanism.
all_names: Causal mechanism linking action to stated goal
Traces a causal chain from provision to effect

species.name: Concrete regulatory text or numeric threshold proposed
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment identifies a specific provision (section number, CFR cite, or clause) of the proposed rule and proposes exact substitute language, a specific numeric threshold, or a specific edit. A 10: names the exact provision and gives drop-in replacement text or a specific number. A 0: comment does not engage with the rule's actual text or numbers at any level of specificity.
species.rationale: R04 proposes an exact clause to add to the monograph and a specific limit ('Extractant Insoluble Material... Not more than 2 g/kg'), R28 picks a specific numeric standard ('the lowest proposed threshold of 0.018 mg/L') among named alternatives, and R54 requests removal of an exact phrase from a cited subsection (296.21(c)). These are drafting-grade contributions that a topic/sentiment checklist cannot distinguish from a vague comment like R01, which never touches the rule's text.
all_names: Concrete regulatory text or numeric threshold proposed

species.name: First-hand experiential grounding with checkable specifics
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the commenter grounds their position in their own direct, checkable stake or observation (a named location, date, incident, or role they personally experienced) rather than a generic expression of concern. A 10: specific personal facts (address, date, named event) that tie the commenter's position to something verifiable. A 0: comment expresses concern or support with no personal, checkable detail -- it could have been written by anyone about anything similar.
species.rationale: R55 gives a specific address two blocks from the Superfund site and describes personal exposure to the plume; R36 identifies the specific site, notes reliance on private wells versus the already-treated municipal supply, and names farms/livestock as an affected category from local knowledge. Contrast R23, whose 'we urge... keep it closed' carries no personal or locally-specific fact, despite similar topic and length.
all_names: First-hand experiential grounding with checkable specifics
First-hand situated account of how the rule lands

species.name: Engages the countervailing consideration or concedes a point
species.instruction: Score whether the comment shows awareness of the strongest consideration running against its position and argues through it rather than around it: a constraint the agency faces, a benefit of the proposal it still opposes, a cost of the alternative it recommends. A 10 states the countervailing consideration accurately and explains why the recommendation survives it. A 5 acknowledges the other side in passing without engaging it. A 0 presents the question as one-sided. Reward genuine grappling; a ritual 'while I appreciate the agency's efforts' earns nothing.
species.rationale: R30 concedes that budget neutrality requires offsetting reductions and then argues that these particular offsets are misplaced given progress-report workload; R33 concedes that adding photographs is both inevitable under IRTPA and long overdue before attacking the implementation; R14 opens by saying the writer would normally be entirely supportive; R26 proposes bismuth citrate as a substitute and then volunteers its encephalopathy risk before moving to other alternatives. R12 and R45 treat their questions as having no other side.
all_names: Explicit engagement with tradeoffs or counterarguments
Engages the countervailing consideration or concedes a point

species.name: Substantive on-topic focus on the actual rule
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the entire comment substantively addresses the specific proposed rule or notice at hand, versus drifting into unrelated political commentary, personal attacks on other commenters, or grievances that don't bear on the rule's content. A 10: every substantive sentence is about the proposed action itself. A 0: the comment is primarily about something else entirely (an unrelated political figure, an attack on another submitter) with no engagement with the rule's substance.
species.rationale: R37 is not a comment on the rule at all but an ad hominem attack on a different commenter ('you are not helping your cause... don't behave like a terrorist'), and R45 is a political rant about 'President Tiny Hands' and 'the blue wave' with only a one-line nod to the actual listing decision -- both dense_low_card_high, i.e., the scorecard rates these highly (likely on length/citation-adjacent features) while missing that they barely engage the rule. Contrast R42, which stays on the FWS experimental-populations rule throughout a long, substantive letter.
all_names: Substantive on-topic focus on the actual rule

species.name: Verifiable, attributable evidentiary sourcing
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether factual claims used to support the comment's position are attached to identifiable, checkable sources (named studies, agency data, statutes, official reports) as opposed to vague, unattributed, or dubious sourcing (unnamed blogs, hearsay, 'as I understand it'). A 10: specific citations to checkable sources that actually support the claim made. A 0: confident factual claims with no source, or sourced to non-authoritative/unrelated material.
species.rationale: R02 supports its recommendation with a numbered reference list including a named 2000 systematic review (Stead et al.) and FDA compliance-check data, and R41 cites the specific Medicare Benefit Policy Manual chapter and section it is interpreting. Contrast R43, which supports its urgency claim about airbag injuries with a pedestrian-fatality statistic from an unrelated context sourced to 'Darrigo and Diaz Attorney and Law' and a blog post ('TrueLaw.com') -- confident-sounding citation apparatus that doesn't actually check out.
all_names: Checkable sources that actually support the claim made

species.name: Argumentative coherence free of non-sequiturs
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment reads as a single coherent line of argument without abrupt, irrelevant insertions that break the logical thread. A 10: fully coherent from start to finish. A 0: contains a jarring non-sequitur or unrelated insertion that has nothing to do with the surrounding argument, undermining trust in the rest of the text.
species.rationale: R38 is an otherwise coherent public-health explainer on vaccination that is abruptly interrupted by 'check animals for aids check animals for aids feline is the one I think giving ainds to citizens please test our animals' -- a non-sequitur that has nothing to do with the surrounding vaccine text or, seemingly, the docket. R43 similarly cites an unrelated pedestrian-fatality statistic inside an airbag-inflator comment, breaking the argument's internal logic. A checklist scoring topic-relevance or length would not catch this loss of coherence within an otherwise on-topic document.

species.name: Quantified scale of real-world impact
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment supplies specific, position-relevant numbers (dollar figures, percentages, counts, timeframes) that establish the scale of the problem or benefit the rule addresses. A 10: concrete, comment-specific figures that make the magnitude of the issue legible. A 0: no numbers at all, or only a generic/borrowed statistic not tied to the specific matter at hand.
species.rationale: R29 gives a specific import figure ('over 200 million pounds of equivalent fruit') driving its market-restriction argument, and R51 supplies a chain of concrete figures (50 million boxes, 27% production decrease, $760 million in damages, 45,422 jobs) tied directly to the size-requirement rule it's commenting on. Contrast R01, which cites only a generic, non-localized UN statistic ('over 1 million species will go extinct') that isn't tied to the specific listing decision, and R23, which offers no numbers at all.

species.name: Analytic application of stated professional expertise
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether a commenter who identifies professional experience or expertise actually puts that expertise to analytic use on the rule's specifics, versus merely stating a credential or role without further application. A 10: the stated expertise is visibly doing analytic work (e.g., applying billing codes, engineering knowledge, or procedural experience to critique or reshape the rule). A 0: a credential or role is mentioned but the ensuing argument does not draw on it in any demonstrable way.
species.rationale: R41 (an occupational therapist) applies detailed knowledge of specific CPT billing codes and RVU mechanics to argue against a payment cut, and R50 (a 43-year pilot) uses direct certification-process experience to design a specific alternative credentialing mechanism. Contrast R19 ('as a frequent user of cosmetic and hair products, I support this proposal') and R56, where a stated identity or credential is not followed by any analytic use of it -- these should not receive credit merely for asserting a role.
all_names: Analytic application of stated professional expertise

species.name: Concreteness of the specific request or decision sought
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment identifies a clear, actionable decision the agency should make, as opposed to a vague sentiment with no operational content. A 10: names a specific decision or action for the agency to take. A 0: expresses only a general feeling or explicitly disclaims having any specific recommendation.
species.rationale: R54 requests a precise word-level edit, and the NMDA letter (R58) requests specific reinstated language mandating direct notice to governments. Contrast R25, which explicitly states 'we have no specific recommendations but encourage the Secretary to take all reasonable measures,' and R59, which describes an expected attitude toward claimants but names no actual decision for the agency to make -- both should score low here regardless of how professionally the surrounding text reads.
all_names: Concreteness of the specific request or decision sought

species.name: Presence of an original articulated stance or recommendation
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the commenter states an actual position, judgment, or recommendation supported by their own reasoning, as distinct from passively presenting or reproducing informational/source material without adding interpretation. A 10: a clear original stance backed by the commenter's own reasoning. A 0: no discernible stance from the submitter at all -- the text is a reproduction of another document (e.g., an agency's own guidance text) with no interpretive commentary layered on top.
species.rationale: R08 is, on inspection, simply the FDA's own draft guidance document reproduced verbatim (title page, contact info, table of contents, boilerplate 'this guidance... does not create or confer any rights') with no visible stance, request, or reasoning contributed by whoever submitted it -- yet it sits in the dense_high_card_low slice at a high dense percentile (.846), suggesting the dense model may be responding to its technical/official register rather than to any actual argument. Contrast R04, similarly long and technical, but which contains clearly original requests ('Add the following clause...', specific proposed limits and rationale) -- real substantive content behind the formal register.
all_names: Presence of an original articulated stance or recommendation

species.name: Reasoning about operational or implementation consequences
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment reasons through how the rule would actually function in practice for the people who must carry it out or live under it -- workload, timing, second-order/ripple effects -- rather than stopping at top-line support or opposition. A 10: traces a specific practical consequence of implementation with enough detail to be actionable. A 0: no reasoning about how the rule would work in practice at all.
species.rationale: R60 explains specifically why a 14-day withdrawal-reporting window would consume instructors' time that would otherwise go to teaching and grading, and the Ohio EMA letter (R40) walks through, by page and line, how specific guidance language would prevent otherwise-reimbursable pre-award costs. Contrast R09 and the EDF template letters (R14, R26), which take a position on the rule but never reason about how compliance or rollback would actually play out operationally.
all_names: Reasoning about operational or implementation consequences

species.name: Detail-level concreteness of any proposed alternative
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether, when the comment proposes an alternative approach, the mechanism is specified in enough detail (steps, components, numbers, procedure) that someone else could implement or evaluate it -- versus a vague gesture toward an unseen or undescribed solution. A 10: a fully specified alternative mechanism laid out in the text itself. A 0: an alternative is mentioned in name only, or the commenter points to a solution that exists outside the comment ('I already have one, contact me') without describing it.
species.rationale: R50 lays out a fully specified alternative certificate mechanism (8-year passport-like document, embedded chip, sticker-based rating updates, reissue cadence) that a reader could evaluate on its own terms. Contrast the emergency-management THIRA/HIRA comment (R44), which gestures at 'an innovative hybrid risk assessment... I have already produced a one stop shop format... feel free to reach out if interested' -- a solution-shaped comment that provides no actual detail within the text itself, which a checklist rewarding 'proposes alternative' as a topic tag would likely over-credit.
all_names: Detail-level concreteness of any proposed alternative
Proposes an alternative specified well enough to draft

species.name: Differentiated identification of affected stakeholder groups
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment identifies which specific populations or entities are affected by the rule and distinguishes how the impact differs across them, rather than referring only to an undifferentiated 'the public' or 'everyone'. A 10: names at least two distinct affected groups and explains how the rule's effect on them differs. A 0: refers only to a single undifferentiated affected group or does not identify who is affected at all.
species.rationale: R36 distinguishes municipal water customers (already served by a treated supply) from private-well-dependent households and separately from farms/livestock as affected categories with different exposure pathways, and the DHS public-charge comment (R46) distinguishes the green-card applicant from citizen children in the household, quantifying the latter (15.4 million children) as a distinct affected population. Contrast R23 and R30, which refer only to an undifferentiated 'general public' or 'all students' with no breakdown of who bears the impact and how.
all_names: Differentiated identification of affected stakeholder groups

species.name: Personal narrative fused with policy-actionable specifics
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on the INTERACTION of two properties together: (a) the comment includes a genuine personal/professional narrative, AND (b) that narrative is tied to specific, policy-actionable facts (a named incident, date, or mechanism) that could inform the agency's decision. A 10: both are present and fused -- the personal account supplies the concrete facts driving a specific request. A 0: either the narrative is present but generic/unmoored from any specific fact (sentiment-only), or specific facts are present with no narrative or interpretive voice at all (a bare document reproduction).
species.rationale: R21 fuses a nurse's 20-year professional narrative with a named 2018 Delaware ethylene-oxide release incident and specific resulting requests (fenceline monitoring, multilingual notification), and R36 fuses local knowledge of a specific site with concrete facts about private wells and farms. This is a genuinely composite property distinct from C03 or C11 alone: R01 has narrative without specific facts (scores low), while R08 has policy-relevant technical content without any narrative or interpretive voice (also scores low) -- only the fusion of both should score high, which helps separate the strongest dense_high_card_low rows from ones that only partially resemble them.
all_names: Personal narrative fused with policy-actionable specifics

species.name: Supplies new decision-relevant facts not already in the record
species.instruction: Score how much genuinely new, decision-relevant information the comment puts in front of the agency: facts, quantities, field observations, records, market conditions, or local circumstances that the proposal itself does not contain and that bear on whether the rule is right. A 10 states specific new information the agency plausibly did not have, tied explicitly to why it matters for this decision (e.g., a volume figure that changes the market picture, a physical fact about the equipment, a described exposure pathway the proposal omits). A 5 adds a modest amount of information that is real but marginal or already implied by the proposal. A 0 contains no information the agency did not supply: it restates the proposal, expresses a preference, or recites general background. Judge information content, not confidence or credentials.
species.rationale: The dense-high rows repeatedly carry an informational payload the scorecard appears to ignore: R14 reports roughly 200 million pounds of equivalent fruit arriving as European/Turkish concentrate and argues the proposal is unaware of it; R37 reports that many households near the Blades site are on private wells and that farms water crops and livestock from local sources; R02 supplies the fact that fusible plugs were only installed with certain early-generation composite reservoirs phased out in 2003-2004. Against these, R32 is scored high by the dense model but contains no information at all beyond a restatement of the proposal, so this criterion also usefully separates the informative dense-high rows from the empty ones.
all_names: Supplies new decision-relevant facts not already in the record

species.name: Engages a named provision, alternative, or solicited question
species.instruction: Score whether the comment fastens onto something specific in the proposal (a section, a defined alternative, a numeric threshold, a phrase, a question the agency expressly asked) AND says what is wrong with it or answers it. Both halves are required: a 10 both identifies the exact target and gives a reason or an answer, so the agency could act on the comment without guessing which provision is at issue. A 5 identifies a target with only a bare preference attached, or gives reasoning that never lands on a locatable part of the proposal. A 0 addresses only the general subject matter of the rulemaking. Pinpointing alone, with no stated reason, does not earn above a 4.
species.rationale: R44 quotes the Department's own solicited question about whether two centers would be efficient and answers it with reasons about resource duplication and peer learning; R24 chooses among the rule's enumerated alternatives and endorses the specific 0.018 mg/L threshold; R58 targets section 91.818(b) and the word 'measurable' and proposes what should replace it. R35 sits at the top of the scorecard (card_pct=0.994) while engaging nothing more specific than the topic of genetic modification, which is the shape of over-credit this composite is designed to catch.
all_names: Engages a named provision, alternative, or solicited question

species.name: Identifies a false or outdated premise in the proposal
species.instruction: Score whether the comment locates a specific assumption the proposal rests on and shows why it is wrong, no longer true, or does not hold for some class of cases. A 10 names the premise, shows it is mistaken, and draws the consequence for the rule (the requirement is misdirected, the scope is wrong, the effect will invert). A 5 asserts that the agency has misunderstood something without demonstrating it. A 0 registers disagreement with the outcome while accepting or ignoring the reasoning behind it. Reward attacks on the reasoning, not the intensity of the objection.
species.rationale: R02 shows the AD scope assumes fusible plugs are standard components across all inflation systems and demonstrates that this is not the case; R14 argues the market-restriction premise predates a change in import dynamics so that the restriction would subsidize importers rather than growers; R52 shows that the revision would let Handbook guidance operate with the force of regulation, a consequence the notice does not acknowledge. R12 is near the top of the scorecard (card_pct=0.925) while accepting the proposal wholesale and attacking nobody's premises at all.
all_names: Identifies a false or outdated premise in the proposal

species.name: Compliance feasibility grounded in how the work is done
species.instruction: Score whether the comment demonstrates concrete knowledge of what complying would actually require, and uses it to evaluate the proposal. A 10 walks through the real sequence of work, access constraints, staffing, or timing and shows why the proposed requirement is or is not achievable as written, ideally proposing the achievable version. A 5 asserts that something is burdensome or unrealistic without describing the work. A 0 makes a demand with no account of how anyone would carry it out. Detailed knowledge of the operation, not the strength of the complaint, is what is being scored.
species.rationale: R02 explains that the plug cannot be inspected on the aircraft even with a borescope, so each system must be removed, unpacked in a shop, repacked with specialized fixtures, and the reservoir recharged and leak-checked, which is why the 30-day window fails fleet-wide; R08 shows that a 14-day withdrawal-reporting cycle collides with a full teaching load and points to the existing financial-aid reporting dates as the workable cadence; R34 reports that MASH-compliant devices are not getting tested and approved fast enough and that the sunset dates therefore put reimbursement at risk. Nothing in R45 or R56 addresses execution at all.
all_names: Compliance feasibility grounded in how the work is done

species.name: Accurately represents what the proposal says and does
species.instruction: Score whether the comment demonstrates that the writer actually read and correctly understood the proposed action before responding to it. A 10 characterizes the proposal correctly (quoting or paraphrasing it faithfully) and the response is aimed at what the agency actually proposed. A 5 is broadly on target but garbles a material aspect of the proposal or the posture of the proceeding. A 0 misdescribes the proposal, responds to a different action, or contains no engagement with it at all. Text copied from the agency's own document without any responsive content scores 0, since nothing has been characterized.
species.rationale: R44 reproduces the Department's solicitation verbatim before answering it and R24 correctly enumerates the alternatives it is choosing among. At the other end, R54 sits high with the dense model while its entire attachment is the agency's own draft guidance re-submitted with no comment, R11 pastes encyclopedia text on vaccination and appends an unrelated plea about testing animals, and R09 treats a listing docket as the occasion to abolish the statute. This criterion is the main defense against a comment that looks technical because it carries the agency's own vocabulary.
all_names: Accurately represents what the proposal says and does

species.name: Analyzes coverage, population, or time-horizon scope gaps
species.instruction: Score whether the comment reasons about the boundaries of the rule: who or what is swept in that should not be, what is left out that should be in, or over what period the effects and obligations should run. A 10 identifies a specific over- or under-inclusion, says why the boundary is drawn wrong, and indicates where it should sit instead. A 5 hints that the rule reaches too far or not far enough without specifying the boundary. A 0 contains no reasoning about scope. Applies equally to product classes, covered entities, geographies, exposure pathways, and time.
species.rationale: R18 argues that a rule reaching only Salmonella in breaded stuffed chicken leaves Campylobacter and other products uncovered and proposes a class-wide treatment principle instead; R25 argues that the compensation horizon of three or four years is wrong because downstream flood, landslide and debris-flow risk persists for decades; R37 notes the municipal supply is treated while private wells and agricultural water remain outside the monitoring; R02 argues the opposite direction, that the AD scope is broader than the Service Bulletin effectivities warrant. Scope reasoning shows up in dense-high rows across four different agencies.
all_names: Analyzes coverage, population, or time-horizon scope gaps

species.name: Ask lies within agency authority and this proceeding
species.instruction: Score whether what the comment requests is something this agency can actually do in this rulemaking, and whether the comment shows awareness of the legal or programmatic frame. A 10 grounds the request in the statute, the agency's authority, or the posture of the proceeding, and asks for something within it. A 5 asks for something the agency could plausibly do but shows no awareness of the constraint. A 0 asks for relief the agency cannot grant here (repealing its authorizing statute, actions by other branches or bodies) or otherwise misapprehends what this docket decides. Score the fit of the request to the forum, not its merits.
species.rationale: R49 argues from what the ESA does and does not require, citing 16 U.S.C. 1539(j)(2)(A), and asks only for language the Service can put in a final rule; R38 argues that the current position departs from the FD&C Act's definition of 'drug', which frames the ask as one FDA can grant; R53 correctly invokes the Mine Act's good-cause extension authority. Against these, R09 asks that the ESA be abolished inside a listing docket and R12 looks to lawsuits, indictments and impeachment, neither of which is relief the agency can grant.
all_names: Ask lies within agency authority and this proceeding

species.name: Substance survives deletion of the position statement
species.instruction: Apply this test: delete every sentence that states support, opposition, gratitude, feeling, or a purely procedural request, and score what remains. A 10 leaves behind a body of reasons, facts, or requested changes that stands on its own as regulatory input. A 5 leaves a thin residue: one reason, or a general consideration. A 0 leaves nothing, because the comment consisted entirely of a position, an attitude, an endorsement of someone else's filing, or a scheduling request. This targets comments that carry every outward marker of seriousness while contributing no content.
species.rationale: R03 says outright that it has no specific recommendations and encourages the Secretary to take all reasonable measures, yet sits at card_pct=0.791; R39 is a map legend and a thank-you at card_pct=0.886; R40 is a statement about how claimants intend to behave toward staff at card_pct=0.886; R53 asks only for sixty more days and says nothing about the training rule's merits. R15, by contrast, survives the deletion almost intact, because each page-and-line item states a problem and the resolution sought.
all_names: Substance survives deletion of the position statement

species.name: Reasons generalize beyond the commenter's own benefit
species.instruction: Score whether the reasons offered would persuade someone who does not share the commenter's stake: is the requested change justified by facts about the regulated activity, or only by what it does for the writer? A 10 supplies a reason stated in general terms that a neutral analyst could adopt, even when the commenter plainly benefits. A 5 mixes a generalizable reason with heavy reliance on the writer's own advantage. A 0 offers the commenter's benefit, record, or convenience as the reason itself. Self-interest is not disqualifying; unexamined self-interest as the whole argument is what scores low.
species.rationale: R47 lays out the operating facts of an airport-within-an-airport (independent ramp, no interline coordination, package rather than belly-baggage handling) so that a flexible SMS rule can be written for that class of situation, not merely for the writer; R48 seeks compliance improvements whose benefit runs to the program. Against these, R07 supports a waiver chiefly by recounting its own grant accomplishments, and R17 asks that anonymous complaints not be counted against servicers on grounds framed entirely around servicer interests; both sit high on the scorecard.
all_names: Reasons generalize beyond the commenter's own benefit

species.name: Disagreement argued against the rule, not against persons
species.instruction: Score whether the comment's force is directed at the proposal and its reasoning rather than at individuals, officials, political figures, or other commenters. A 10 can be sharply and unsparingly critical while every criticism attaches to a provision, a process, or a consequence. A 5 mixes argument with gratuitous characterization of people or motives. A 0 consists substantially of invective, imputed corruption, or attacks on another commenter's character. Bluntness is not penalized; displaced target is.
species.rationale: R08 is blunt about administrators but every objection attaches to the reporting requirement, and R28 is harsh about FEMA's culture while converting the critique into a seven-step redesign of program delivery; both are dense-high, card-low. The three most extreme scorecard over-credits in the slice run the other way: R35 (card_pct=0.994) closes with 'Oh, I forgot... MONEY', R12 (card_pct=0.925) is a string of epithets aimed at officials, and R21 (card_pct=0.897) attacks another commenter's identity and calls her a terrorist. A criterion that separates target from tone would move all three.
all_names: Disagreement argued against the rule, not against persons

species.name: Situated operational knowledge
species.instruction: Score 10 when the commenter’s relevant role is paired with concrete observations, practices, or cases that illuminate how the rule operates; score 0 when credentials or affiliation appear without operational evidence.
species.rationale: R08 describes the actual physical inspection and repacking process, and R55 explains the unusual airport-within-an-airport operating environment at Memphis.

species.name: Cross-system spillover analysis
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies plausible effects across connected systems, sectors, or regulatory objectives and explains their connections; score 0 when it discusses only an isolated preference.
species.rationale: R29 explains how production restrictions could alter import prices, storage costs, and grower returns, while R57 connects citrus rules to jobs, transportation, tax revenue, nutrition, and local economies.

species.name: Concrete Distributional Effects
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies specifically affected or vulnerable groups, describes their exposure or access pathway, and connects that pathway to a regulatory choice; score 0 for generic references to the public or fairness.
species.rationale: R30 explains how TIN language can deter farmworkers from obtaining coverage, and R43 identifies assistive-technology implications for students with disabilities; R11 similarly specifies private-well users and agricultural operations.

species.name: Risk-calibrated scope
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment matches regulatory coverage to the actual risk population, component, condition, or setting and explains boundary conditions; score 0 when it seeks blanket coverage or opposition without analyzing scope.
species.rationale: R08 distinguishes affected fusible-plug configurations from systems that never used them, and R12 explains why retaining two differing standards would create specific compliance and liability problems.

species.name: Implementation burden realism
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment explains concrete staffing, timing, equipment, workflow, or cost constraints and relates them to implementation; score 0 when burden is asserted only as inconvenience.
species.rationale: R08 details aircraft removal, unpacking, specialized fixtures, recharging, and repacking, while R19 links a reporting deadline to instructors’ teaching and grading workload.

species.name: Operationally testable definitions
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment converts an ambiguous term or standard into a measurable threshold, decision rule, example, or verification method; score 0 when it merely calls for clarity.
species.rationale: R50 proposes numerical sonic-boom thresholds to replace “measurable,” and R27 identifies conflicting passages and asks how loss-of-life benefits should be calculated.

species.name: Comparative tradeoff analysis
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment compares plausible alternatives, states their advantages and disadvantages, and explains why the preferred option performs better; score 0 when it presents only a categorical conclusion.
species.rationale: R10 compares procedural reforms for exceptional-event demonstrations, while R26 contrasts testing, validated treatment, and broader pathogen-control approaches.

species.name: Temporal and cumulative effects
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment analyzes delayed, repeated, cumulative, or long-term effects rather than only immediate impacts; score 0 when its reasoning is confined to a short-term assertion.
species.rationale: R24 discusses cumulative reimbursement pressures and future access to therapy, while R45 explains why wildfire-related downstream risks may persist for decades.

species.name: Monitoring and Verification Design
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment proposes measurable monitoring, testing, reporting, feedback, or verification that would reveal whether the regulatory approach is functioning; score 0 when it asks for protection or compliance without a way to assess it.
species.rationale: R13 calls for validated and verified controls, while R35 proposes real-time fenceline monitoring and public notification; these add operational observability absent from R57’s request for unspecified measures.

species.name: Program interoperability
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment explains how the proposal should coordinate with existing programs, jurisdictions, standards, or information systems to reduce gaps or duplication; score 0 when it treats the rule as isolated.
species.rationale: R32 connects freight designations to state plans, partner nominations, statutory factors, and multimodal data, while R38 proposes one risk-assessment structure serving several emergency-management programs.

species.name: Legal-technical coherence
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies a specific conflict, assumption, statutory boundary, or inconsistency and reasons through its practical significance; score 0 when it relies on legal or technical language without applying it.
species.rationale: R12 compares the proposed rule with statutory authority and prior regulatory treatment, while R27 points to contradictory page-and-line provisions and incompatible calculation tools.

species.name: Mechanism-to-Remedy Chain
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies a concrete problem, explains its causal mechanism, and proposes a remedy targeted to that mechanism; score 0 for an unsupported preference with no causal explanation.
species.rationale: R11 connects contamination pathways to testing and safe-water measures, while R13 links poultry controls to multiple pathogen risks; these go beyond the generic support in R26 and R57.

species.name: Traceable Evidence
species.instruction: Score 10 when relevant facts, measurements, records, citations, or clearly identified firsthand observations support the claims and their limits; score 0 for slogans, speculation, or unsupported assertions.
species.rationale: R35 supplies incident details and cited studies, while R58 supplies a concrete analytical procedure; this separates evidence-based input from assertions in R37 and R44.

species.name: Operational Knowledge Generalized
species.instruction: Score 10 when firsthand or professional experience is translated into a recurring implementation problem and a rule-level implication, rather than left as an isolated anecdote; score 0 when experience is absent or merely narrated.
species.rationale: R25 converts occupational-therapy practice into a reimbursement recommendation, and R35 converts clinical experience into facility-monitoring safeguards; R57 offers affected-community perspective but no comparable generalizable recommendation.

species.name: Feasible Implementation Design
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies who would implement the change, the practical constraints, and a workable adjustment that preserves the regulatory objective; score 0 when it demands action without implementation analysis.
species.rationale: R14 explains instructors’ reporting capacity and offers a workable schedule, while R17 describes inspection logistics and a narrower compliance path; these reveal a dimension not guaranteed by detailed institutional submissions such as R06.

species.name: Second-Order Consequences
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment traces credible downstream effects on markets, behavior, institutions, or related populations and explains the causal path; score 0 when it discusses only the immediate effect.
species.rationale: R27 explains how a production restriction could subsidize imports and depress growers’ returns, while R51 explains how splitting support centers could reduce peer learning and increase overhead.

species.name: Regulatory Coherence
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies a concrete conflict, gap, overlap, or interaction with existing law, standards, programs, or guidance and proposes a coherent resolution; score 0 when outside authorities are merely mentioned.
species.rationale: R47 distinguishes guidance from regulation and addresses notice authority, while R23 identifies internal guidance conflicts and incompatible calculation practices; the criterion rewards explaining why the interaction matters.

species.name: Constructive Counterargument
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment acknowledges a plausible opposing consideration or preserves a useful part of the proposal, then explains a focused modification; score 0 when it offers only unconditional praise, rejection, or attack.
species.rationale: R27 begins from ordinary support but explains why new import information changes the analysis, and R28 supports the rule while limiting out-of-range introductions to justified cases; this contrasts with polemical submissions such as R44.

species.name: Administrable Legal Precision
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment links its recommendation to governing authority or defines a clear, consistently applicable decision rule, threshold, or term; score 0 when legal language is invoked without an administrable implication.
species.rationale: R24 recommends a specific contamination threshold among defined alternatives, and R50 replaces an ambiguous sonic-boom term with a measurable standard; this captures usable precision beyond formal legal citations in R29.

species.name: Decision-Relevant Novelty
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment contributes material information, context, or an affected operating environment not apparent from the proposal and explains why it changes the analysis; score 0 when it repeats the proposal, supplies boilerplate, or merely endorses another submission.
species.rationale: R09 explains the unusual airport-within-an-airport operating environment, and R27 introduces import data that changes the market analysis; R54, by contrast, largely endorses another party’s comments without adding substance.

species.name: Calibrated Uncertainty
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment distinguishes established facts from assumptions, states relevant contingencies or limitations, and keeps its recommendation proportional to the evidence; score 0 when it overclaims, treats uncertainty as certainty, or makes unsupported universal demands.
species.rationale: R18 identifies reliability and privacy limitations in location data, while R28 conditions translocation on exhaustion of native-range options; this distinguishes disciplined analysis from categorical claims in R37 and R44.
